data.consequences: tests/test_repo_is_generic.py and tests/test_local_layer.py fail any change that commits a private host, a reviewer block, or re-ignores gates.toml. This machine's gates.toml and reviewers.toml moved to .ddflow/local/ (2026-09-30). A clone still holding a machine-local .ddflow/gates.toml sees it as untracked: move it to .ddflow/local/.
data.context: Supersedes D-no-own-services-committed, which named .ddflow/gates.toml as a git-ignored local file while gates.toml is also the only supported place to declare human gates (bug B-gates-toml-dual-role); init never ignored a top-level reviewers.toml (bug B-init-ignore-local). Operator 2026-09-30: correct both.
data.decision: Committed files carry generic project policy only. Reviewer endpoints, model names of a private deployment, API-key variables, LAN hosts/IPs and machine-specific sizing (test worker counts) go in git-ignored local files: .ddflow/local/config.toml, .ddflow/local/gates.toml, .ddflow/local/reviewers.toml (read last, so they win), an untracked .roborev.toml, .claude/settings.local.json. A top-level .ddflow/reviewers.toml is ignored too, as a guard. .ddflow/gates.toml is NOT ignored: it is where a project declares its gates, human=true checkpoints included, which must reach every clone. Task bodies, research records, lessons and commit messages refer to such a service by role, never by address. ddflow RECOMMENDS services; it never ships one person's configuration. History is not rewritten.
data.title: Nobody's own services are committed; machine-local config lives under .ddflow/local/, and .ddflow/gates.toml is committed project policy
